messages.content: Docs for GitHub Copilot currently talk about copilot-instructions.md. A reviewer asked whether Copilot also writes other artifacts under .github/, and this thread never recorded the layout we used for that integration.
Update the documentation so the GitHub Copilot integration describes the full GitHub-specific artifact layout, not only the instructions files.
GitHub Copilot artifacts in this repo are documented in both .github/instructions and .github/skills — include both directories when you mention the integration.
Update the documentation so the GitHub Copilot integration describes the full GitHub-specific artifact layout, not only the instructions files.
The hero currently only names Claude Code and never says we are open source. Marketing asked us to match the positioning from the last homepage copy review.
Update the home page so the hero matches the team's landing-page positioning, including how we describe licensing and which agents we support.
Homepage convention: mention the project's open-source status prominently and cover all supported AI coding agents, not only Claude Code.
Update the home page so the hero matches the team's landing-page positioning, including how we describe licensing and which agents we support.
That sentence still looks like a fixed Claude-centric file checklist. I want it to reflect every agent and artifact type the evaluator actually detects.
Rewrite the homepage sentence that lists AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, copilot-instructions.md, and SKILL.md so it matches the coverage we actually ship.
Homepage decision: describe all detected files and artifacts and all supported agents, including GitHub Copilot, Claude, and Cursor, rather than only a fixed file list.
Rewrite the homepage sentence that lists AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, copilot-instructions.md, and SKILL.md so it matches the coverage we actually ship.
RemediateTab still shows Generate Prompts in the toolbar. I remember we debated keeping it as an alternative path versus removing it from the module UI.
Apply the team's last product decision about the Generate Prompts control on the remediation module.
Team decision: the remediation module must not show a Generate Prompts button.
Apply the team's last product decision about the Generate Prompts control on the remediation module.
ContextTab modals still use Browse, and the tree badges say Rule and Skill with no agent name. I keep mixing that with the newer copy.
Align the Context tab modal buttons and tree badges with the terminology we standardized for that tab.
Context tab convention: modal buttons say Display all; generic labels get an agent prefix (for example Claude Rule); Browse is deprecated.
Align the Context tab modal buttons and tree badges with the terminology we standardized for that tab.
prompt-generator still emits every instruction as a flat numbered list. Nested expected behaviors end up on the same line as the parent step.
Generated SKILL.md files with nested steps are hard to scan. Update the skill-instruction templates and tests so nested details stay readable.

Skill template convention: keep instructions concise and verb-first; when a step has sub-steps or expected behaviors, render indented sub-bullets. Edit getSkillInstructions in prompt-generator.ts, update snapshots, then run bun test and bun lint.
Generated SKILL.md files with nested steps are hard to scan. Update the skill-instruction templates and tests so nested details stay readable.
The Cursor run control starts the agent, but the command string is truncated or hidden until after the process starts.
When the frontend runs a Cursor remediation, users still cannot inspect the exact CLI invocation. Fix the display and add coverage.

Cursor remediation workflow: locate the CLI invocation in RemediationRunner.tsx, show the complete command before execution with wrapping for long text, then run the Cursor-agent frontend tests so the visible command matches the actual invocation.
When the frontend runs a Cursor remediation, users still cannot inspect the exact CLI invocation. Fix the display and add coverage.
The runner still schedules every evaluator even when inventory already shows the project has no matching artifacts. I do not want a broad optimization sweep.
Evaluator runs still execute checks that the technical inventory says are irrelevant, and empty-result paths stay expensive. Tighten that path only; leave unrelated optimizer work alone.

Optimization scope: skip evaluators from technical inventory checks in the runner; the empty-result fast path is Optimization #6 in docs/OPTIMIZATION.md. Keep parallel execution order and error isolation. Do not broaden into cache-prefix work.
Evaluator runs still execute checks that the technical inventory says are irrelevant, and empty-result paths stay expensive. Tighten that path only; leave unrelated optimizer work alone.
Each evaluator block still inlines full SKILL.md files, and the shared project files appear after the per-evaluator text, so the prefix keeps changing.
Evaluator prompts are too large and cache hit rates are poor because shared context is not stable across calls. Shrink the prompts and add tests.
Prompt-cache workflow: keep only skill frontmatter in evaluator file blocks, put shared file content and project context first as a stable prefix, then verify cache breakpoints and prompt tests.
Evaluator prompts are too large and cache hit rates are poor because shared context is not stable across calls. Shrink the prompts and add tests.
A sample repo without a documented layout still gets a raw directory listing back from remediation, with no hint what each folder is for.
Project-structure remediations still dump bare folder names. Change the prompt and test so the tree is actually usable.

Project-structure rule: read standards/project-structure.md, require an annotated directory tree with a short purpose for every directory, wire it through the evaluator prompt, and verify with a missing-structure sample that bare listings no longer appear.
Project-structure remediations still dump bare folder names. Change the prompt and test so the tree is actually usable.
History cards dump every file action in one stack. Rules, skills, and context updates are mixed, and expanding a row still fights with the status counts.
The remediation Action Summary is still a flat list. Redesign it so reviewers can scan file actions by type, then add frontend coverage.

Action Summary workflow: group entries into Rules, Skills, Context, and Other; show path, issue/action details, and status in a three-column table; keep addressed/skipped counts and expandable diffs; check grouping and truncation on a narrow layout.
The remediation Action Summary is still a flat list. Redesign it so reviewers can scan file actions by type, then add frontend coverage.
The persistent plan footer and the pre-execution plan both bury the totals. Zero-count rows currently look like missing UI rather than an actual zero.
Reviewers cannot see how many standards versus skills a remediation plan will touch. Make those counts obvious in both plan views and cover empty states.

Remediation plan convention: clearly label standards, skills, and other output counts in both the persistent and execution plan sections, keep zero-count states readable, and add frontend tests that the labeled counts match the plan.
Reviewers cannot see how many standards versus skills a remediation plan will touch. Make those counts obvious in both plan views and cover empty states.
People keep pasting the documented Cursor example into tickets. That is not necessarily what RemediationRunner invoked for this run.
Cursor remediations fail with a generic toast. I need to know what command the frontend actually sent so we can tell whether the failure is ours or the provider's.
Cursor diagnostics convention: when a remediation fails, show the exact CLI command the frontend invoked, not a rewritten example from the docs.
Cursor remediations fail with a generic toast. I need to know what command the frontend actually sent so we can tell whether the failure is ours or the provider's.
The README still treats remediation as a single 'run the agent' step. People keep asking what actually happens after they click run, and which artifacts they should review.
Expand README.md so newcomers can follow the web remediation flow end to end, including how many AI stages run and what kinds of file changes come back.
Remediation documentation convention: describe the four phases (plan/execute errors, then plan/execute suggestions) and that results include file changes plus reviewable output.
Expand README.md so newcomers can follow the web remediation flow end to end, including how many AI stages run and what kinds of file changes come back.
A 2M-line customer repo burned cloud quota last week. We only have a vague instruction to cap resource use; I need the concrete reject-before-queue procedure.
Cloud evaluations of huge repositories still start expensive work before we refuse them. Guard that path and add tests without changing local runs.
Cloud policy: reject repositories over 1M lines before expensive evaluation, return a stable actionable error, keep local mode unchanged, and test below, equal-to, and above the threshold.
Cloud evaluations of huge repositories still start expensive work before we refuse them. Guard that path and add tests without changing local runs.
Investigate the SSE connection leak in src/api/sse/progress-handler.ts and fix it with a regression test.
Add a configurable nested SKILL.md depth option to src/shared/file-system/skills-finder.ts and cover the default and custom-depth behavior with tests.
Add conservative LLM-generated verbal-bloat detection as evaluator section 10.4, update coverage documentation, and add tests for the prompt guidance.
Fix UnifiedFileRow so an expanded remediation row shows its action issues and the diff together, then run tests and verify collapsed behavior.
The README Remediation section still reads like a single click-run step. Expand it so a newcomer can follow what actually happens after they start a web remediation.
Add a local-execution warning to the remediation confirmation modal that shows each provider's write command and security implications, while hiding it in cloud mode.
Add provider-specific lightweight model support and use it for linked-document summarization, with type, unit, and provider tests.
Propagate verbose logging through DocsFinder linked-document summarization so provider process messages appear when verbose mode is enabled; update tests.
Investigate the SSE connection leak in src/api/sse/progress-handler.ts.
Add a nested SKILL.md depth option to src/shared/file-system/skills-finder.ts.
